data.title: Quote
data.tagline: A sourced quotation or excerpt set apart from the surrounding text
data.description: Use indentation, quotation marks, or a rule to separate an expert’s words or customer feedback from an author’s view. Keep the speaker, source, or needed context; do not style ordinary text as a quote just for decoration.

distinctions.label: Typography
distinctions.explanation: Quote is sourced or deliberately highlighted original wording. Typography is the overall system of text hierarchy and style.

use: A direct quote in an article
avoid: Every paragraph styled as a quote
Someone else’s view with no source or context
A fictional person, publication, or review

lessonPractice.title: An article highlights a customer's exact words about their experience. How can it avoid becoming decoration or fabricated endorsement?

options.label: Keep the original words and identify the authorized speaker, source, and necessary context
options.feedback: A quote separates original speech from the author's view, while source and context let readers judge what it represents.

options.label: Choose a powerful sentence, add quotation marks, and omit who said it or where
options.feedback: Quotation styling does not make content verifiable. Without a source, readers cannot know whether the words are real.

options.label: Rewrite the idea to sound stronger and add a generic avatar and job title
options.feedback: Rewriting and inventing identity changes the evidence, so it can no longer be presented as the customer's exact words.

data.agentPrompt: Present this customer's exact words as a quote without rewriting. Show the authorized name, role, source, and necessary context. If source or permission is missing, mark it for confirmation rather than generating an avatar, title, or metric.
